questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I love the nature up north, so a place where i had easy access to mountains, forrests and lakes was important to me

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I had no issues finding the required information, but a checklist or something of the sort could be helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were meetings held that one could attend.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was not hard per say, but you do need to look around to find places that have furnished/semi-furnished apartments with a lease less than a lear. 3015 Sherbrooke st. W is quite close to campus and have some solid prices for pretty modern apartments. Landlord is nice too.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: call people! thats how i got my apartment, since my landlord made an exception and allowed me to lease the apartment only for the time i was there instead of a full year

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Registration is on a first come, first serve basis, so you have to be ready and have in mind which classes you want as soon as registration opens.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: zoom meetings explaining the process step by step

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: There was one class i did not get first try, but grabbed a spot later down the line.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: if you do not get your classes first try, dont stress! if you check every now and then over the next week, a space is usually freed up that you can grab.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: some of the courses could be quite challenging, but the more challenging courses were often the ones with the best professors in my experience.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: you are graded continuously, instead of having one big final exam at the end.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
BIOL 352
CHEM 302
COMP 204
MIMM 324

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: BIOL 352 was hands down the most fun and interesting course during my exchange. unique concepts not taught many places, as well as fun lab dissections. MIMM 324 was too hard for me, as i realised i did not have the necessary prior knowledge to excel this course. Despite this, i would recommend the course as it had the smartest and kindest professor i have had during my studies.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: too many too count, i was part of the climbing and outdoor clubs

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: go outdoors! so many beatuful places to see and experience.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: go up to mont royal for a walk, mile-end for food and culture trip. go outside the city and go camping!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: although knowing some french was helpful, you could go through you entire exchange speaking only english and be fine.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: the tipping culture was hard to understand for someone who is not used to it, as there are a lot of unwritten rules.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: i enjoyed how friendly and laid back people are, despite the bustling city life. also the older parts of the city had a edge to them that was different from what i was used to

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: be prepared to be graded continuously, try poutine at least once and find time ind your schedule to take some daytrips

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
if you are able to, get a bike. although the infastructure is not as good as denmark, it is still a viable way to get around. you can find some cheap on
kijiji.ca

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: biking around the city and learning the ins and outs of the city. at the end of my trip, when i finally could remember different street names, places and stores without needing to use google maps, i felt like i had gotten a lot out of my stay.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: being graded continuously felt very overwhelming at times, especially in my CHEM course where i had bitten off more than i could chew

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
